headline: 叔父さん is 叔父 (oji) plus さん (san).
アンテナ is borrowed from English “antenna”.
全, “all, whole, entire”, comes from Middle Chinese 全 (dzjwen, “complete, whole”).
スプーン is borrowed from English “spoon” and first attested in 1860.
票, “label, ballot, sign”, is traced to Middle Chinese 票.
シーズン is the English word “season” in katakana.
パイロット is the English word “pilot” in katakana.
どうぞ is どう (“how, anyhow”) plus ぞ, an emphatic particle.
テント is the English word “tent” in katakana.
刺す, “to sting, to bite, to stab”, is cognate with 指す and 挿す, which are also read sasu.
マスク is borrowed from English “mask”.
戻る, “to return”, is a doublet of 悖る (motoru, “to go against”).
ファックス is borrowed from English “fax”.
問う was spelled inconsistently in Old Japanese literature, as both to₁pu and to₂pu.
ガム, “chewing gum”, is borrowed from English “gum”.
サイレン is borrowed from English “siren”.
問い, “question, query”, is the continuative stem of the verb 問う (tou).
メモ, “memorandum, note”, is the English word “memo” in katakana.
放送 is a wasei-kango compound of 放 (hō, “release”) plus 送 (sō, “send”), attested in the mid-Taishō era.
スリッパ, “slippers”, is the English word “slipper” in katakana.
溶く, “to dissolve (paint)”, is cognate with 解く (toku).
クリーニング, “dry cleaning”, is borrowed from English “cleaning”.
ドレス is borrowed from English “dress”.
そっと was originally そと, and the source calls Italian “sotto” a false friend.
バンド is the English word “band” in katakana.
楽, “comfort, ease”, is borrowed from Middle Chinese, where the source writes it 樂 (MC lak).
カー is the English word “car”, borrowed as it is.
遅れ, “delay, lag”, is the continuative stem of the verb 遅れる (okureru), with examples from at least the 1300s.
レクリェーション is borrowed from English “recreation”.
点々 is a reduplication of 点.
コンクール, “contest”, is from French “concours”.
